title: One claim, four desks
objective: Learners follow one health claim across the desks that touch it (member, intake, adjudication, payment and, if it comes to that, appeals) and see that most of the elapsed time is waiting between desks, not work at them, and how the route, the reviewers on duty and the outcome change the picture.

recommended.why: A swimlane diagram puts each step in the lane of whoever does it, so the hand-offs and the waits between desks are the picture, which is what process owners argue about.

alternative.why: The swimlane shows who and in what order; a Gantt timeline per lane shows how long, with the waits as the empty stretches. Which one convinces a process owner that the queue, not the review, is the problem?

assumptions: Durations are illustrative business days for a fictional health plan; no benchmark, contract or real system is implied
The claim always passes intake validation; the lesson is about time, not edits
Auto-adjudication prices the claim in minutes; manual review pends in a queue that the reviewers on duty share, so the wait is 5 days divided by the number of reviewers, then one day of review
Approved and overturned claims wait for a weekly payment run (3 days) and letters take 2 days in the mail
An appeal takes the member 2 days to file, waits 5 days for a clinical reviewer, takes 6 days to review and is overturned; a denial without an appeal ends with the letter
Events happen one after another; nothing runs in parallel
units: time: business days from the visit
playback: 24 s for the whole claim, so a day is shorter on screen when the claim takes longer
checkDescription: Events run back to back and work plus waiting equals the elapsed time; the appeals lane is used only when the claim is appealed and the payment lane only when it is paid; manual review adds a pending wait of 5 days divided by the reviewers, automatic adjudication adds none; playback markers are ordered.

learnerPrompts.predict: Set the reviewers on duty to 5 before you play. By how many days does the claim get paid sooner, and which single bar changes?
learnerPrompts.explain: With the claim denied and appealed, the member waits weeks and the desks work for only a few days in total. Where would you put one more person, and why is the answer not "adjudication"?
